name: Tieraxo Asset Booster
author: Rob Art

sections.description:
Find the right file faster. Keep your WordPress Media Library organised. Fix media problems without the repetitive work.

As your website grows, so does your Media Library. Hundreds of images, documents and other uploads become difficult to find, check and maintain. Tieraxo Asset Booster adds practical media management tools directly to the WordPress screens you already use, without replacing your library or changing how your files are stored.

Create colour-coded folders, filter files by type or condition, identify oversized images and missing alt text, inspect file statistics, edit attachment details in bulk, and replace images without starting again.

What you can do with the free plugin

  • Organise files into folders and subfolders. Create colour-coded folders, add private notes, drag media into folders and place the same item in multiple folders. Organising does not move the underlying files.
  • Find images, videos and documents quickly. Filter by type and format, upload date, attachment status, legacy format, oversized images or missing alt text. Filters work across your library in grid and list views.
  • Spot issues with File Analytics. See the breakdown of your media, identify large files, check missing alt text and review format and metadata reports. Export reports as CSV files.
  • Edit alt text, captions and descriptions in bulk. Update attachment information in one place with inline editing and automatic saving. Improve consistency without opening every file individually.
  • Manage titles and repair thumbnails. Edit media titles in bulk, rebuild missing thumbnail sizes and generate additional resized copies. The title editor does not rename physical files.
  • Swap or relink media. Replace an existing file while keeping its address, rename files and update supported references, or switch references to a different image already in your library. Review a dry-run before making changes.
  • Keep media URLs flexible. Use the reversible, on-the-fly Media URLs tool to serve domain-independent links when moving between site addresses.
  • See your library at a glance. A dedicated dashboard and WordPress dashboard widget display useful media statistics and shortcuts to tools.

Media folders without moving your uploads

Tieraxo folders are an organisational layer, not physical directories. Keep your existing URLs and file locations, make subfolders, assign one of ten colours and work from both the Media Library grid and list. Folder-filtered views can also be bookmarked. Deleting a folder does not delete the media assigned to it.

More useful filters where you actually work

Use Quick Filters to narrow down files by category and subtype, recent uploads, attached or unattached status, and common media issues. Tieraxo also extends the standard Add Media picker, so you can use folder and quick-filter controls while inserting assets into posts and other supported standard media-picker interfaces.

File Analytics that lead to action

Instead of guessing where media problems are, open reports covering missing alt text, large files, image formats, metadata weight and library health. The Formats inventory identifies modern, legacy, vector and supported file types. Export the results to CSV, then jump to relevant Fixers where available.

Bulk fixes and safer file replacement

Use Fixers to maintain alt text, captions, descriptions and titles, or rebuild thumbnail sizes in batches. Swap & Relink offers several replacement and renaming workflows, including a dry-run of affected references. Supported references can include content, featured images, galleries, widgets and common integrations. Complex stored page-builder data may be left untouched for safety and reported, so always review the preview and keep a backup before major changes.

Tieraxo also supports a workflow with RobArt Image Guard for swapping a protected image into an existing placement.

Need more? Tieraxo Asset Booster Pro adds advanced media tools

The free plugin includes folders, quick filters, analytics, bulk editors, thumbnail regeneration and Swap & Relink. The optional Pro add-on introduces more demanding tasks:

  • Bulk Image Optimiser: convert supported images to WebP or other server-supported formats, compress them, adjust quality and optionally resize.
  • Unused Media: review potentially unused attachments and selectively move items to the Trash, with safeguards for assets you want to keep.
  • Metadata slimmer: review and remove selected embedded EXIF, GPS, IPTC and XMP data.
  • Smart Search and Dominant Colour: find images by dimensions and filter a scanned library by colour.
  • Advanced filters: combine additional size, dimension and condition criteria.
  • Upload Triage: review incoming media and apply naming, folder and alt-text choices during upload.
  • Additional clean-up tools: including orphaned resized-file pruning and selected advanced folder actions.

Important: Image conversion and bulk compression are Pro features, not features of the free plugin. Free users can still identify large or legacy-format images and take action using the included organisational and maintenance tools.

Set up in minutes

Install and activate Tieraxo Asset Booster, then open Media > Library. Your existing grid and list views gain new folder and filter controls. Visit Tieraxo Asset Booster in the admin menu for File Analytics, Fixers, the Dashboard and Settings. No shortcodes or front-end redesign required.

External services

Tieraxo Asset Booster does all of its work on your own site and server. It makes no automatic network requests during normal use, and sends no analytics or tracking data anywhere.

It contacts one external service, and only when you actively ask it to:

  • robart-illustration.eu (Tieraxo licence & Pro download API) — if you choose to upgrade and enter a Tieraxo Asset Booster Pro licence key, the plugin sends that licence key, your site URL, and the plugin slug to https://robart-illustration.eu/ to validate the key and download the Pro package. This happens only when you click to activate a licence — never on a normal page load, and never for users who do not upgrade. The service is operated by Rob Art. See the Privacy Policy (https://robart-illustration.eu/privacy-policy/).

No other external services are contacted.

Uninstall

Tieraxo Asset Booster preserves your data by default. Deactivating the plugin keeps everything, and even deleting it keeps your settings and folders — so reinstalling picks up exactly where you left off.

If you turn on “Remove all data on uninstall” in Settings before deleting the plugin, uninstalling removes everything it stored:

  • Its settings, licence record, install date, review-prompt state and database-version marker (stored as options).
  • Its cached values (transients).
  • Its folder structure — the folder taxonomy terms and their assignments.

Your media files are never touched either way — removing the plugin’s folders only removes the labelling layer, not the images. It writes nothing outside your own site.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/tieraxo-asset-booster, or install it from the Plugins screen in your WordPress admin.
  2. Activate it through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Open your Media Library — you’ll see the new folder and filter controls on the toolbar. The Tieraxo Asset Booster admin menu gives you the Dashboard, File Analytics, Fixers and Settings.
sections.faq:
Do I have to change how I use the Media Library?

No. As soon as you activate Tieraxo Asset Booster the Media Library gains folders, quick filters and a toolbar — in both the grid and list views. There is nothing to shortcode or wire up.

Does organising into folders move or change my files?

No. Folders are a labelling layer on top of your existing library — filing an image into a folder never moves or renames the file on disk, and deleting a folder never deletes the images inside it. An image can belong to more than one folder at once.

Will it work with my theme or page builder?

Yes — it enhances the standard WordPress Media Library screens (grid and list), so it works regardless of your theme. Builders that render their own custom media UI instead of the standard library may not show the extra controls there.

Is renaming a file safe? Won’t it break links?

The Swap & Relink tool renames the file and all its thumbnail sizes, then rewrites every reference to it across your posts, pages and custom fields. Complex saved data from some page builders (serialized/JSON blobs) is deliberately left untouched to avoid corrupting it, and it’s reported so you know. A dry-run shows exactly how many references will change before anything is written.

Does it send my data anywhere?

No. The plugin’s library tools run on your own site, and it does not send tracking or usage analytics to an external service. The only external request it ever makes is to validate a Pro licence and download the Pro package — and only when you actively enter a licence key. See the “External services” section for details.

What does the Pro upgrade add?

Pro adds bulk image conversion and compression, Unused Media review and clean-up, metadata slimming, Smart Search by dimension, Dominant Colour filtering, advanced multi-axis filters and Upload Triage. Folders, basic filters, File Analytics, core Fixers and Swap & Relink remain available in the free version.

Does deleting the plugin remove its data?

Only if you ask it to. By default your folders and settings are kept, so reinstalling picks up where you left off. Turn on “Remove all data on uninstall” in Settings first if you want a clean removal. Either way, your media files are never touched. See the “Uninstall” section.
sections.changelog:
0.1.10

  • Improved: Swap no longer switches on WordPress’s Bulk Select, so the “Delete permanently” bar no longer appears and the image you pick is not left ticked. While Swap is open, click an image (or press Enter on it) to swap it.
  • New: each image you swap shows a “✓ Swapped” badge until you close Swap, so a run of swaps is easy to follow.
  • Improved: Swap from library and Rename now check what will change by themselves. A note above the buttons says what will be updated (green), or warns when nothing uses the image (amber, and Swap stays off). No more separate “Check what will change” click.
  • Improved: keyboard support. Enter presses the main button (Swap, Swap everywhere or OK), Esc closes the swap window and, with no window open, ends swap mode.
  • Improved: the “File successfully swapped” message closes by itself after a moment.

0.1.9

  • Fixed: in the Optimiser, the “to optimise” tally now counts up as convertible images are found during the scan (recent uploads are checked first), instead of only appearing at the end.
  • Fixed: after an optimise run finishes, the panel now returns to its clean starting state (progress bar and file list cleared), keeping only the “Optimised N · saved” confirmation.
  • Fixed: file names containing special characters (such as the × sign) no longer show their raw HTML code in the Optimiser list.
  • Fixed: spreadsheet and document files (XLSX, XLS, DOCX, PPTX, PDF and more) now show a clean file-type badge in the Media grid instead of a long raw format string.

0.1.8

  • Security: internal hardening.

0.1.7

  • Security: internal hardening.

0.1.6

  • Fixed: converting an image to another format (for example JPG to WebP) left the old-format sizes in the uploads folder, where nothing used or removed them. The Optimiser (Pro) now removes the files the new version no longer uses, including sizes no longer made after a resize, and keeps a large upload’s full-size original attached.
  • Improved: Prune orphans (Pro) also finds the old-format sizes left behind by earlier conversions, unless another image of that name still uses them.

0.1.5

  • Fixed: image dimensions in the Swap panel and Upload Triage could show a long decimal (for example “1791.818 × 1123.636 px”), because the browser sometimes reports a fractional size for a loaded image. They are now rounded to whole pixels.
  • Fixed: activating a Pro licence failed, because the licence and download service moved from robsnow.eu (no longer online) to robart-illustration.eu. Tieraxo now uses the new address, and the readme, Upgrade page and sidebar links point there too.
  • Fixed: in the “Add media” window, Tieraxo’s folder controls overlapped WordPress’s own toolbar at the bottom of the window. They now sit in one tidy row beside it.

0.1.4

  • Changed: the folder allowance and the analytics scan size are now the same for every install and are not tied to any tier or licence. Both are generous usability defaults and can be raised or removed with the tiax_folder_cap and tiax_fa_scan_cap filters. No folder is ever locked. Pro adds separate tools (Optimiser, cleanup, Upload Triage and more); it does not lift these limits.
  • Fixed: corrected the Terms and Privacy links in the readme.

0.1.3

  • Fixed: the sticky column header on the Fixers editors (Alt Text, Filename, Caption / Description) now pins flush to the top of the scrolling list. It previously sat about 16px down, letting the first row peek above it, because the scroll area’s card padding offset the sticky position.

0.1.2

  • Fixed: the Caption / Description bulk editor table layout — the File column no longer stretches to fill the row and squash the Caption and Description editors into a thin strip on the right. The columns now have sensible widths and the description box shows two lines so its text isn’t clipped.

0.1.1

  • Fixed: the “Oversized” condition filter now works in the Media Library grid view. It previously did nothing there — the grid loads its media over AJAX, and the size filter was written for the list view’s page load, so in grid view it let every image through instead of narrowing to the oversized ones. It now filters correctly in both grid and list views (and shows an empty result when nothing is oversized, like the other condition filters).

0.1.0

  • Added: swap an on-page image for a different one straight from your Media Library. Open the swap panel, choose “Choose from library”, pick the replacement, and every place the old image appeared — content, featured images, Elementor, WooCommerce galleries and widgets — is updated to the new one in a single step. A read-only check first shows how many places will change before anything is saved, and the old image stays in your library.
  • Added: RobArt Image Guard compatibility. Protect an image with Image Guard first, then use the library swap to replace your existing unprotected image with the protected version, in place — no delete, re-upload and re-protect cycle. The protected image’s secure delivery and right-click protection carry across the swap.

0.0.28

  • Fixed: after swapping an image, the new picture now appears immediately for visitors. A swap keeps the same filename (so links don’t break), which meant browsers and CDNs kept showing the old cached image; the swapped image’s URLs now carry a version marker so they refresh straight away.

0.0.27

  • Under the hood: the File Analytics library query now binds its row limit through a prepared statement, and the readme is marked tested up to the current WordPress version. No visible change.

0.0.26

  • Changed: the Media Library grid filter bar is more compact — smaller dropdowns so the filters, size controls and search sit on one line again at a normal window width instead of wrapping to two.
  • Changed: in the “Swap a file” panel, the bracketed explanations under each option now sit on their own line, so the controls no longer stretch across a wide row.
  • Changed: the Advanced Filters “Apply” and “Clear” text buttons are now compact icon buttons (funnel and mop), and the folder dropdown is trimmed to match the other filters.

0.0.25

  • Changed: SVG images are now included in the “missing alt text” check and the missing-alt badge, so the badge agrees with the “No alt text” library filter — SVGs carry alt text and it matters for accessibility and SEO.
  • Under the hood: stopped loading empty Pro admin style/script scaffolds, and made the Pro update check fail faster and cache a down server’s response for longer so it can’t slow the admin.

0.0.24

  • Fixed: the “Missing alt” and “Large files” counts are now accurate for big libraries (they were capped at 1,000 / a partial total), and the bulk alt-text editor counter now ticks down correctly as you add alt text instead of jumping to a wrong number. The dashboard figure updates immediately whenever alt text changes anywhere — the editor, the Media Library or elsewhere.
  • Fixed: the “Potential saving” tile on File Analytics now opens the Optimiser instead of blanking the page.
  • New: choose how the Media Library grid loads — WordPress 7.1’s infinite scroll (default) or a paged grid with a “Show: N” control, so a very large library stays manageable. Set it under Library View.
  • New: Pro updates now install through WordPress’s own Updates screen (for licensed sites, from the licence server).
  • Improved: full translation template covering every screen, including Pro.

0.0.23

  • New: Tieraxo now works inside the “Add media” picker (the media window that opens when you insert an image into a post, product or SEO field), not just the full Media Library. A folder dropdown lets you jump straight to a folder, the quick filters (type and condition) narrow the grid, Smart Search finds images by SKU / filename or size (Pro), and each thumbnail shows its file-type badge and pixel dimensions — so you can find the right image by eye while inserting.

0.0.22

New: the Folder Panel gained a large default folder allowance that keeps the folder bar quick to scan. It applies the same to every install and can be raised or removed with a filter. No images are ever affected by it.
Improved: folder lists now sort naturally, so “Folder 2” comes before “Folder 10”. The recent date-range filter now reads in chronological order.
Fixed: pressing Cancel while swapping a file now closes the whole “Swap a file” panel instead of leaving it open. The Colour Index report now refreshes automatically when a scan finishes.

0.0.21

Hardening pass for WordPress.org compliance and code quality — no change to how any feature works. Tightened output escaping and input sanitising across the admin screens, moved the Pro-only tools cleanly behind the add-on so the free build ships only its own features, and standardised the internal Pro-tier check. Removed a few unused placeholder folders.

0.0.20

  • New welcome screen: the first-run splash is now a proper welcome card — what the plugin does, the feature list, and one-click routes to Settings or the Dashboard. Also fixed the splash sometimes never appearing after activation.
  • The plugin Dashboard is now a real overview: live library stats (items, size, missing alt, large files, unattached, folders), a tools grid linking every section, your latest uploads, and a mini guide explaining what each tool does for your site.
  • A matching at-a-glance widget on the main WordPress Dashboard, with quick stats that link straight to the tool that acts on them.
  • File Analytics — Formats is now a full inventory: every common image, document, video, audio and archive format grouped with a status (Modern / Legacy / Vector / Supported), how many you have, and a recommended conversion for legacy formats.
  • Settings rebuilt as a clean card layout: System Info, tool directory, licence, a new “Remove all data on uninstall” option, and a Danger Zone reset. Uninstalling now keeps your data unless you opt in to removal.
  • New in Pro: “Hide empty formats” — the file-type filter only lists formats your library actually contains, updating itself automatically.
  • Polish throughout: brand green ticks on all-clear states, consistent Pro pills on locked tabs, capped scrolling editor tables with pinned headers, standard switches everywhere, per-page sidebar descriptions, matching icons per section, and a Get Pro link on the Plugins screen.
  • Fixed: clicking a locked Pro report tab no longer swaps its card for a generic “Report” panel; the toolbar folder/swap icons sit in the same place on Free and Pro in list view; the folder icon now highlights on rollover; sort arrows on the flag columns sit beside the label.

0.0.19

  • Upload Triage (Pro) now applies your choices for real: on upload each file is renamed on disk (and its title updated to match), filed into the folder you pick, given the alt text you type, and marked as reviewed. The new file appears in the library straight away, in its folder.
  • New Triage settings: choose which checks appear, set a default folder for new uploads, require a file to be marked reviewed before it can upload, and set your own large-file and maximum-dimension thresholds.
  • The Triage “New file name” field now selects just the name (not the extension) ready to type, and blocks invalid characters live — lowercase, hyphens, no spaces.
  • Standardised the upgrade experience: a two-column upgrade window and a branded “Upgrade to Pro” card at the foot of every sidebar, plus a compact plan panel on the Dashboard.
  • Fixed: Media Library folder counts could drift after adding or deleting files, which affected folder filtering. Counts are now kept accurate.
  • Tidied the advanced filter bar labels so the row fits on one line.

0.0.18

  • Fixed: the pixel-dimensions caption under Media Library grid tiles wrongly showed “Not available” on the main Media Library screen. It now reads each image’s size correctly, and only shows “Not available” for files that genuinely have no dimensions (such as some SVGs).

0.0.17

  • New Upload Triage (Pro) — early foundation. When turned on (its own menu page has the on/off switch), adding a file to your Media Library now opens a Triage window first: the upload is genuinely held before anything transfers, so you can review it and choose to upload it or cancel — and cancelling adds nothing to your library. Works from the grid, the “Add Media File” button, and the media window inside a post. The review actions (route to a folder, label, optimise, flag) are being built on top of this next.

0.0.16

  • Internal code organisation (no change to how anything works): the Fixers page was split into smaller per-tab files for maintainability. Under-the-hood housekeeping ahead of release.

0.0.15

  • Internal code tidy-up (no change to how anything works): consolidated repeated logic into shared helpers — the backup-confirmation guard on destructive actions, byte-size formatting, the Pro upsell card, and the lazy-loading grids all now use single shared functions. Purely under-the-hood housekeeping ahead of release.

0.0.14

  • New Optimiser — its own menu page for converting and compressing images in bulk. Convert to WebP (and other formats your server supports), set a quality level, optionally cap the width and strip hidden data — all in one pass. Set a global default, then fine-tune any image on its own row with per-image format and quality.
  • The review list shows a thumbnail, current size, and an estimated saving per image, so you can see at a glance which files are worth optimising before you run anything.
  • File Analytics gains a Potential saving overview card — an at-a-glance estimate of how much space a default optimise pass would reclaim across your library.
  • The Fixers Broken Records tab now lets you review and delete orphaned library entries (records whose file is missing from disk) right there, with each record re-checked at the moment of deletion so nothing live is removed.
  • CSV export is expanded: alongside the existing report datasets, you can now export a full library report (one row per image, with columns you choose — including used/unused, metadata weight and estimated saving) and an all-files-on-disk report that lists every image file including generated sizes and orphaned files.
  • Estimates across the Optimiser and File Analytics now correctly skip files that are already in the target format, so projected savings are honest.

0.0.13

  • New Unused Media tool (Pro) in Fixers: scans your whole library for files that are not referenced anywhere — no post, page, custom field, widget or setting. Each result shows a thumbnail and its file size, so you can see exactly what you are about to remove.
  • Pick what to clear with per-row checkboxes (and a Select all), then move only the selected files to the Trash — recoverable — behind a backup confirmation. Nothing is removed unless you deliberately choose it.
  • Mark false positives as used: a Keep action on any row (and Keep all) tells future scans to leave that file alone — handy when a plugin or theme uses an image in a way we can’t detect. A Kept items manager lets you review and un-keep at any time.
  • The Media Library gains an Unused only filter (in the advanced filter panel) that shows just the files the last scan found unused.
  • New Metadata slimmer tool (Pro) in Fixers: removes hidden data from images — camera settings (EXIF), GPS location, captions/keywords (IPTC), editing history (XMP), colour profile and the embedded thumbnail. Tick exactly what to remove and keep the rest (for example, keep copyright or the colour profile). Scan shows the reclaimable weight per image; stripping rewrites the originals and regenerates thumbnails, behind a backup check.
  • The Attachment Details panel now has a Swap & Relink button that opens the Swap window for that image directly.
  • Fixes: corrected the unused-media check so an image is no longer counted as “used” by its own stored data.

0.0.12

  • The Regenerate Thumbnails tab is clearer and does more. It’s now built around three plain actions: Rebuild resized copies (re-create the full set for images that are missing sizes or have broken data), Add a new size (generate one extra copy at a width you choose and add it to every image), and Prune orphaned copies (remove leftover resized files at sizes nothing uses any more).
  • Rebuild now shows the exact set of image sizes registered on your site, so you can see what a rebuild will (re)create instead of guessing.
  • Add a new size is width-based: you set the width and each image’s height follows to keep its shape, with a live example showing what your images become. Originals are never changed and images already narrower are skipped.
  • Prune (Pro) scans your uploads for orphaned resized files, shows how much space you’d reclaim with a live progress bar, lists them, and deletes them safely behind a backup confirmation. The full list is shown in a compact two-column layout to save space.
  • Advanced filters: you can now filter the Media Library by folder. The folders you already organise your media into appear as a dropdown in the advanced filter panel and narrow the grid or list instantly.

0.0.11

  • Rename a file and keep everything working: the Swap window’s “Replace and update the name” mode now renames the file (and all its thumbnail sizes) and rewrites every link to it across your posts, pages and custom fields, so nothing breaks. Complex saved data (from some page builders) is left untouched for safety.
  • Before renaming you can “Check what will change” to see how many links will be updated — nothing is changed until you confirm.
  • You can also drop in a brand-new image while renaming — including changing its type, for example a PNG to a WebP — and it will re-encode, rebuild thumbnails, and update all the links in one go. The window tells you clearly when the file type is changing.
  • The new file name is pre-filled with the current name, so if you’re only changing the file type you can leave it as-is.
  • Drag and drop to organise: drag an image (or several selected images) from the grid straight onto a folder tag to file it there.
  • Fixes: the Swap window now blurs the page behind it, no longer opens the built-in image editor when you pick an image, keeps its drop area visible, and refreshes the affected image on screen after a swap or rename. The drag preview now shows a single clean thumbnail.

0.0.10

  • Swapping a file now works. Choose “Just replace the file”, drop in the new version, and it overwrites the file in place — keeping the same name and web address — then rebuilds the thumbnails. There’s an option to also set the date to today.
  • To keep things safe, the new file has to be the same type as the one you’re replacing (for example a WEBP for a WEBP). If it isn’t, you’ll be told to use rename mode instead.
  • After a successful swap you get a clear “File successfully swapped” confirmation, and the image updates on screen straight away.
  • Tidied the Swap settings row so the options use the full width, with the root-relative-links note sitting neatly under its own option.

0.0.9

  • The Swap window now has a proper preview step. Choose an image to swap and you’ll see the current file on the left and a drop-zone for the new file on the right, each with its dimensions, size, type and web address shown underneath.
  • The new-file side updates as soon as you drop or choose a file — it shows the image, its filename, and how the web address will change (or that it stays the same).
  • Added a header bar in the brand colour, and an option to store links as short root-relative paths when you also rename the file.

0.0.8

  • Renamed the plugin to Tieraxo Asset Booster throughout — menu, screens, onboarding and settings — with its own logo now shown in the admin header, the menu, and the setup wizard.
  • New Swap button in the Media Library toolbar (grid and list views), sitting next to the folder button. It opens its own panel, ready for the upcoming swap-a-file / rename-a-file tools; the panel is a placeholder for now.
  • Tidied the Media Library toolbar so the folder, swap and advanced buttons line up evenly, and every drop-down panel now shares one consistent look and sits flush under the toolbar.

0.0.7

  • Folders now work in the Media Library list view (the table view), not just the grid. The folder bar appears at the bottom, with a folder button in the top toolbar next to the Advanced filters — the same layout as the grid.
  • Click a folder to filter the list to it; the address updates so the view is bookmarkable.
  • File images into a folder from the list: tick the rows you want (using the list’s own checkboxes), and the move button lights up — pick a folder to file them.
  • New “Folder” column in the list view showing each image’s folder(s) as coloured tags. Click a tag to filter to that folder.

0.0.6

  • Folders: drag to reorder. Reorder folders by Alt-dragging the pills on the bottom bar, or by dragging them in the new “Folder Order” list on the Folder Panel settings page — sub-folders reorder within their own parent, and the order you set now shows everywhere in the Media Library.
  • Folders: per-folder Settings window — rename (with a length cap), assign one of ten colour tags (shown on the folder everywhere), add a private note, and archive or delete. Pro adds move/re-parent, merge, a per-folder roll-up override and “empty folder”. Folders render in their chosen colour throughout, and you can jump to any folder from a “Go to” list.
  • File Analytics: new “Metadata Weight” report — finds images carrying heavy embedded data (camera info, GPS, editor leftovers) as a share of the file, so you can see where the bloat is. The report is free; the slimming action is planned for Pro.
  • File Analytics: orphaned records (a library entry whose file is missing from disk) now have their own count on the overview and a safe bulk-delete — each file is re-checked at the moment of deletion, so a record whose file is still present is never removed. A clear warning and tick-to-confirm gate it.
  • Fixers: new “Caption / Description” tab — fill in image captions and descriptions in bulk, saving automatically as you type. New “Regenerate Thumbnails” tab — rebuild missing or broken image sizes in safe batches with a progress bar; the original file is never touched. New “Broken Records” tab links through to the analytics clean-up.
  • Diagnose → act: File Analytics tabs now show a “Fix this” button in the sidebar that jumps straight to the matching fixer (e.g. Missing Alt Text → the bulk Alt Text editor). The attachment screen also gains a “Change in bulk” link under the Alternative Text field.
  • Fixes: tab order in the bulk editors now skips the small “open in editor” link, so Tab moves cleanly between fields. The Fixers sidebar text now updates correctly when you switch tabs. Images that are vector graphics (SVG) are no longer wrongly flagged as missing thumbnail sizes.

0.0.5

  • Folders: organise the Media Library into folders, the un-bulky way. A folder button in the grid toolbar opens a slim panel to create folders (with an optional parent); once you have a folder, a sticky bar appears at the bottom of the screen showing your folders. It collapses to a small circle to get out of the way, and stays where you leave it.
  • Folders: hover a folder with sub-folders to peek its tree; click a folder to show only its images; click again to show everything.
  • Folders: file images into folders — click the move button (uses WordPress’s own Bulk Select), tick the images, then pick a folder. Images can live in more than one folder at once.
  • Folders: a Settings window to rename and delete folders (deleting a folder never deletes the images), plus a visual folder Map (Pro) — a tree diagram of your whole structure; click any folder in the map to jump straight to its settings.
  • Folders: new “Folder Panel” menu item under Lib View with an on/off switch for the whole feature.
  • Fixers: new “Media URLs” tab — make media links domain-independent so moving the site to its live address can’t break them. A safe on-the-fly toggle (reversible, nothing changed in the database) plus a Pro option to rewrite them permanently, with a backup check and a clear warning first.
  • Fixers: new “Filename” tab — give images clear titles in bulk (edits the title only; the file on disk is never renamed).
  • Grid toolbar: the tile-size control and the Advanced/folder buttons now use clear icons with consistent rollover behaviour; the Advanced and folder panels both stay pinned in view as you scroll.

0.0.4

  • Smart Search (Pro): type a dimension and the search understands it — an exact size (1200×1200), a single edge (500), a comparator (>2000, <200), or an approximate (~500). Plain words still search filenames as before; a hint above the box shows how your query was read.
  • Dominant Colour (Pro): scan your library once and then filter images by colour. A hue-spectrum slider (drag a pointer, widen the band) with live per-colour counts and a neutrals row, plus a colour-breakdown chart on the settings page. Colour detection now favours the subject over the background, so a garment wins over the sky behind it.
  • Advanced filters panel (Pro): stackable multi-axis filtering — file-size range, dimension range, and the legacy/oversized/missing-alt conditions — all in one row alongside the colour control. Conditions update live; Clear resets them.
  • File Analytics: a new menu section (right after the Dashboard) — a media overview with a type breakdown chart and at-a-glance counts, plus reports for missing alt text, large files, format usage and library health. Heavier reports (unused files, duplicates) are Pro and load on demand, and everything exports to CSV.
  • Fixers: a new menu section for fixing issues in bulk, one tab per tool. Bulk Filename/Title editor and bulk Alt Text editor — thumbnail, inline field, auto-saves as you go. The filename editor changes the title only and never renames the file on disk, so nothing breaks.
  • Onboarding: the setup wizard can now run the first colour scan during install, with a safeguard for very large libraries.
  • Performance: File Analytics now loads its page quickly and fetches the slow scans only when you open their tab.
  • Fixes: cleared a stuck colour-scan state that could block a rescan; made the red “Clear” button readable (white text on red).

0.0.3

  • Filter Fix: new free Quick Filters on the Media Library bar — a cascading file type → sub-type chooser (Images → JPG/PNG/WebP…), a concise “recent” date range (last 24 hours / 3 / 7 / 30 days, today, yesterday, this session), the legacy/oversized/missing-alt conditions, and attached vs unattached. Works in both grid and list views and filters the whole library, not just loaded items.
  • Tidier filter bar: shorter labels, tighter spacing, and the sub-type chooser sits next to the media-type dropdown. Widened the grid toolbar so all filters stay on one line.

0.0.2

  • Lib View: grid “Show” chooser now reloads at the chosen count, so it works going down (e.g. from All back to 100), not just up.
  • Lib View: list “per page” selector now offers the full range up to All, and stays on the chosen amount after the page reloads instead of resetting.
  • Lib View: media-flag columns (legacy / oversized / no alt) now show a cross instead of a tick, since they mark problems to fix — clearer at a glance.

short_description: Organise your Media Library with folders, powerful filters, file analytics, bulk edits, thumbnail repair and safe image replacement.
description:
Find the right file faster. Keep your WordPress Media Library organised. Fix media problems without the repetitive work.

As your website grows, so does your Media Library. Hundreds of images, documents and other uploads become difficult to find, check and maintain. Tieraxo Asset Booster adds practical media management tools directly to the WordPress screens you already use, without replacing your library or changing how your files are stored.

Create colour-coded folders, filter files by type or condition, identify oversized images and missing alt text, inspect file statistics, edit attachment details in bulk, and replace images without starting again.

What you can do with the free plugin

  • Organise files into folders and subfolders. Create colour-coded folders, add private notes, drag media into folders and place the same item in multiple folders. Organising does not move the underlying files.
  • Find images, videos and documents quickly. Filter by type and format, upload date, attachment status, legacy format, oversized images or missing alt text. Filters work across your library in grid and list views.
  • Spot issues with File Analytics. See the breakdown of your media, identify large files, check missing alt text and review format and metadata reports. Export reports as CSV files.
  • Edit alt text, captions and descriptions in bulk. Update attachment information in one place with inline editing and automatic saving. Improve consistency without opening every file individually.
  • Manage titles and repair thumbnails. Edit media titles in bulk, rebuild missing thumbnail sizes and generate additional resized copies. The title editor does not rename physical files.
  • Swap or relink media. Replace an existing file while keeping its address, rename files and update supported references, or switch references to a different image already in your library. Review a dry-run before making changes.
  • Keep media URLs flexible. Use the reversible, on-the-fly Media URLs tool to serve domain-independent links when moving between site addresses.
  • See your library at a glance. A dedicated dashboard and WordPress dashboard widget display useful media statistics and shortcuts to tools.

Media folders without moving your uploads

Tieraxo folders are an organisational layer, not physical directories. Keep your existing URLs and file locations, make subfolders, assign one of ten colours and work from both the Media Library grid and list. Folder-filtered views can also be bookmarked. Deleting a folder does not delete the media assigned to it.

More useful filters where you actually work

Use Quick Filters to narrow down files by category and subtype, recent uploads, attached or unattached status, and common media issues. Tieraxo also extends the standard Add Media picker, so you can use folder and quick-filter controls while inserting assets into posts and other supported standard media-picker interfaces.

File Analytics that lead to action

Instead of guessing where media problems are, open reports covering missing alt text, large files, image formats, metadata weight and library health. The Formats inventory identifies modern, legacy, vector and supported file types. Export the results to CSV, then jump to relevant Fixers where available.

Bulk fixes and safer file replacement

Use Fixers to maintain alt text, captions, descriptions and titles, or rebuild thumbnail sizes in batches. Swap & Relink offers several replacement and renaming workflows, including a dry-run of affected references. Supported references can include content, featured images, galleries, widgets and common integrations. Complex stored page-builder data may be left untouched for safety and reported, so always review the preview and keep a backup before major changes.

Tieraxo also supports a workflow with RobArt Image Guard for swapping a protected image into an existing placement.

Need more? Tieraxo Asset Booster Pro adds advanced media tools

The free plugin includes folders, quick filters, analytics, bulk editors, thumbnail regeneration and Swap & Relink. The optional Pro add-on introduces more demanding tasks:

  • Bulk Image Optimiser: convert supported images to WebP or other server-supported formats, compress them, adjust quality and optionally resize.
  • Unused Media: review potentially unused attachments and selectively move items to the Trash, with safeguards for assets you want to keep.
  • Metadata slimmer: review and remove selected embedded EXIF, GPS, IPTC and XMP data.
  • Smart Search and Dominant Colour: find images by dimensions and filter a scanned library by colour.
  • Advanced filters: combine additional size, dimension and condition criteria.
  • Upload Triage: review incoming media and apply naming, folder and alt-text choices during upload.
  • Additional clean-up tools: including orphaned resized-file pruning and selected advanced folder actions.

Important: Image conversion and bulk compression are Pro features, not features of the free plugin. Free users can still identify large or legacy-format images and take action using the included organisational and maintenance tools.

Set up in minutes

Install and activate Tieraxo Asset Booster, then open Media > Library. Your existing grid and list views gain new folder and filter controls. Visit Tieraxo Asset Booster in the admin menu for File Analytics, Fixers, the Dashboard and Settings. No shortcodes or front-end redesign required.

External services

Tieraxo Asset Booster does all of its work on your own site and server. It makes no automatic network requests during normal use, and sends no analytics or tracking data anywhere.

It contacts one external service, and only when you actively ask it to:

  • robart-illustration.eu (Tieraxo licence & Pro download API) — if you choose to upgrade and enter a Tieraxo Asset Booster Pro licence key, the plugin sends that licence key, your site URL, and the plugin slug to https://robart-illustration.eu/ to validate the key and download the Pro package. This happens only when you click to activate a licence — never on a normal page load, and never for users who do not upgrade. The service is operated by Rob Art. See the Privacy Policy (https://robart-illustration.eu/privacy-policy/).

No other external services are contacted.

Uninstall

Tieraxo Asset Booster preserves your data by default. Deactivating the plugin keeps everything, and even deleting it keeps your settings and folders — so reinstalling picks up exactly where you left off.

If you turn on “Remove all data on uninstall” in Settings before deleting the plugin, uninstalling removes everything it stored:

  • Its settings, licence record, install date, review-prompt state and database-version marker (stored as options).
  • Its cached values (transients).
  • Its folder structure — the folder taxonomy terms and their assignments.

Your media files are never touched either way — removing the plugin’s folders only removes the labelling layer, not the images. It writes nothing outside your own site.
